EC2 Instance Launches, AWS services that instantiated new instances, as well as services such as DataSync or AWS Backup which require new instances to support data transfers to or from the US-WEST-2 Region were affected. Our engineers were automatically engaged and immediately began investigating the root cause. We identified the issue to be caused by a subsystem that supports EBS Volumes required during instance launch. We began remediation of that issue at 3:20 PM, and completed full recovery at 4:21 PM. The issue has been resolved and all AWS services are now operating normally.

Incident began at 2026-10-19 23:00 and ended at 2026-10-20 05:08 (all times are US/Pacific ).
Incident Report
Summary
On Monday, 19 Oct 2026 at 22:53 US/Pacific (Tuesday, 20 Oct 2026, 06:53 BST), a data center facility that hosts europe-west2-b, a zone within the europe-west2 cloud region, experienced an external electrical power disruption. This resulted in service unavailability for workloads located in this zone. The subsequent failover of these workloads to unaffected zones and alternate regions caused transient latency and elevated error rates across the broader europe-west2 region.
The resolution of the main impact was completed within 6 hours and 8 minutes.
Root Cause
Facility architecture and background:
The data center facility in the UK region hosts Cloud clusters serving the europe-west2-b zone, which form part of the multi-zonal europe-west2 Cloud region. The site relies on a 2N utility power architecture—where the facility has complete duplicate power paths for every critical load—backed by a central high-voltage generator bank managed by a dual-redundant Programmable Logic Controller (PLC).

The service's Redis client retried aggressively and redialed those connections. That produced a connection storm that saturated the gateway, with about 90% of connection attempts failing. Other services sharing the same network path were degraded as well.
We mitigated the incident by removing the affected resources from rotation, which ended the connection storm and allowed the gateway to recover. We have already reduced the number of connection retries in the impacted service and are further improving retry behavior with jittered backoff, shorter connect timeouts, and retry budgets. We are also working with our infrastructure team to make GitHub more resilient to gateway maintenance.

Resolved - On October 19, 2026, between 15:24 and 16:52 UTC, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, and webhooks generated by Actions were degraded. Live updates on GitHub.com and code search were also degraded for part of this time. No data was lost.
Impact
- Workflow status updates, logs, and checks were delayed.
- 5.13% of jobs on GitHub-hosted runners were delayed in starting, and 0.02% of workflow runs failed.
- During the first 30 minutes, 8.47% of requests to the Actions jobs REST API returned errors.
Pages deployments and webhooks generated by Actions runs were delayed.
An internal Actions service that stores logs and run status lost connections to some of its cache servers in one cloud region and immediately retried them from every server at once. The resulting surge of new connections overloaded a shared network link between our data center and that region, which also disrupted other services that use the same link. We mitigated the incident by moving the Actions service off the affected cache servers and reducing connections from other services on the link. We then processed the delayed Actions work. We are continuing to investigate the cause of the initial connection timeouts.
We were already in the process of rolling out a limit on how quickly this service can open new connections, but it was still in shadow mode (logging only, not enforcing) at the time of the incident. We have since fully enforced it and capped the service's concurrent connection attempts. We are extending these limits to other Actions services, adding backoff to retries, limiting how much shared network capacity a single service can use, and improving alerting so we can find the source of connection surges faster.
